title: PsiSat
subtitle: A 1U gamma-ray burst nanosatellite
summary: A student CubeSat proposal to detect short flashes of high-energy light from orbit, with a compact aluminum shell and six planned electronics layers.
body: Purpose
A scintillator converts incoming gamma rays into light near 550 nm. A sensor reads each flash and a small computer records its timing.
My contribution
I started the project, recruited the team, and wrote the NASA CubeSat Launch Initiative proposal. The shell is modeled in Fusion 360. Jackson Boyle and Christian Tumanda are also on the proposal.
Packaging & status

The target envelope is about 10 x 10 x 11 cm, with mass below 1.33 kg. Six electronics layers are planned. Stage 4 is the power board and Stage 5 holds the batteries; four other boards remain in design. PsiSat has not launched.

title: 3D-printed jet
subtitle: Airframe, propulsion & flight-control development
tools: Fusion 360, Inventor, Ansys Mechanical, Ansys Fluent, PyTorch
summary: A custom printed airframe with twin 80 mm electric ducted fans, developed around structural packaging, aerodynamics, and a target speed above 70 km/h.
body: Airframe & integration
The airplane is drawn in Fusion 360 and printed in separate parts. The wing halves close over a battery bay, while two 80 mm electric ducted fans sit side by side at the rear.
Analysis & control

Structural and flow analysis inform the design. Thrust vectoring and onboard neural-network flight and landing control remain development goals. The 70 km/h figure is a design target, rather than a reported flight measurement.
Explore the model
The original interactive aircraft model and flight demonstration remain available on the main website.

title: Vibration isolation
subtitle: Crystal oscillator mounting study
summary: A modal study of a 10 MHz crystal oscillator on four isolators, identifying the frequency ranges where its mounts amplify or reduce vibration.
body: The assembly
At East End Assemblies, I studied a Wenzel 501-27521-11 oscillator mounted on a plate with four J-3112-2 isolators.
The analysis

I ran modal analysis in Ansys Mechanical and examined the first six natural frequencies. Low modes were near 30-50 Hz, where bench motion can be amplified. Isolation began to help above roughly 70 Hz; the mounts stiffened at higher frequencies.
Engineering purpose
The study described where the mounting system helps and where it does not before installation. These findings apply to the studied assembly and model.

title: Rover structural analysis
subtitle: Frame design, load cases & weight reduction
summary: Design and analysis of the URC rover frame, using static and impact cases to guide structural changes before fabrication.
body: My contribution
I design the URC rover frame in SolidWorks and evaluate it in Ansys Mechanical. LS-DYNA supports short impact cases. Successive load-case iterations reduced the rover mass by 6 kg.
Top-frame study
The September 2026 pass modeled aluminum 6061-T6 members with 5 mm joint connections. Loads of 100 N, 150 N, and 150 N were applied with selected faces fixed. This initial pass used the default mesh.
Design response
Peak deformation on the middle member pointed to the layout as the area to improve. Proposed changes included additional supports, filleted trusses or L-bars, and evaluation of 2 x 2 inch tubing.

title: Batman
subtitle: Autonomous trash-pickup robot
tools: Arduino UNO Q, Ultralytics YOLO11, Python, mecanum drive, TCP / Wi-Fi
summary: A low-cost robot designed to find and collect campus litter, bringing computer vision, omnidirectional motion, and a two-servo claw into one hardware prototype.
body: The idea
Litter collects under benches, beside bins, and along campus walkways. Our team built Batman to explore a small, affordable robot that can reach those spots and pick it up.
See, decide, move, grab

An iPhone streams video to a Windows laptop running a trash-trained YOLO11 model on an RTX 5060. Drive and arm commands travel over TCP on a shared hotspot to the UNO Q. Four motors and two HW-166 (TB6612) drivers power the mecanum base; lift and gripper servos operate the claw.
Integration & lessons

We tested the motors and servos separately before integrating vision. Stable logic power and a common ground resolved driver issues. The stock Zephyr core lacked Servo.h, so the team used soft 50 Hz servo pulses. A shared hotspot replaced campus Wi-Fi for the robot link.
Current state & next steps

The physical base, arm controller, and GPU detector are built. Reliable pickup remains a tuning task: center on detections, improve the grab sequence, tidy the harness, and extend battery runs. Obstacle sensing and onboard compute are future options.

title: MIT Make - Harvard
subtitle: Mobile rover & turret prototype
summary: A wheeled rover carrying a small aiming turret, combining a camera-based recognition system with a compact mechanical assembly.
body: The prototype
The robot combines a wheeled base, a small turret, and a launcher for short 3D-printed cylinders. Camera-based face recognition triggers the prototype behavior.
Mechanical integration
The mechanical task was to package the launcher, aiming hardware, and wiring on a rover that could still move. The photograph documents the bench prototype.

images.caption: Rover and turret on the bench.

title: Thrust vector control
subtitle: Compact rocket steering mechanism
summary: A compact mechanism that steers a rocket by tilting its engine, designed around a roughly 20 x 4 inch, 200 gram vehicle.
body: Packaging & control
Modeled the system in Fusion 360 to fit the actuators, controller, and boards within the rocket. Tilting the engine changes thrust direction to counter disturbances.
Simulation
OpenRocket studies checked system compatibility, center of gravity, and center of pressure to assess the steering design before flight.

title: Hydrogen engine study
subtitle: Comparative performance & operating constraints
summary: An investigation of electrolysis-derived hydrogen in an internal combustion engine, comparing performance and operating demands with gasoline.
body: Research question
Compared engine behavior and operating overhead for hydrogen and gasoline, focusing on efficiency, speed, and thermal demands.
Reported observations

The study reported 40% higher RPM and 60% higher operating temperature for the hydrogen-fueled engine relative to the gasoline baseline. The thermal result motivated closer attention to material constraints.
Design implication
The temperature result highlights thermal management and material constraints as priorities for subsequent investigation.
